verification.note: Confirmed by reading the code. In addons/intelligence/app/file_matching.py:61-73 the addon strips each tag, skips any whose lower() key it has already seen (:65-67), and only then checks the length of the kept tags (:72). In backend/app/routers/internal.py:633-641 the core checks the length of every stripped non-blank tag (:637) before setdefault on tag.lower() (:641). A concrete input where they disagree: U+0130 'İ' is one character, but its lower() is 'i' plus U+0307, two characters. So tags=['İ'*150, 'i̇'*150] produce the same lower() key. The first tag is 150 characters and the second is 300. The addon keeps the first, drops the second as a duplicate, and accepts the filter. The core rejects the second tag for length and answers 422. This breaks I10's 'accept and reject the same inputs'. Reaching it needs unusual Unicode input.

Confirmed. A Grep for straße|STRASSE|casefold across every test*.py finds the parity row only at addons/intelligence/tests/test_filtered_search_contract.py:177-178. backend/tests/test_internal_files_matching.py:228-273 (TestRequestCaps) uses only ASCII tags ('t0'..'t20', 'T0', 'x'*n). No core test checks a pair of tags that lower() and casefold() fold differently, so changing internal.py:641 to casefold() would still pass the core tests.

Same defect as claude-read R2-1. The addon checks length after dedup at file_matching.py:65-73; the core checks it before dedup at internal.py:637-641. They disagree when two tags share a lower() key but have different lengths, for example 'İ'*150 and 'i̇'*150: the addon accepts the filter and the core answers 422.

Confirmed by the same Grep. The fold-sensitive row exists only in the addon's INVALID_FILTERS (test_filtered_search_contract.py:176-179). The core's TestRequestCaps (backend/tests/test_internal_files_matching.py:228-273) uses ASCII tags only.

In docs/specs/filtered-semantic-search.md:172, 'the caps of 10' points to section 10, not to a cap value of 10. Line 359 is the heading '### 10. Non-functional', and line 361 in that section states 'Caps (core and addon, same values): at most 20 tags, each at most 200 characters'. Likewise, 'over the caps in 10' at :219 refers to section 10. These lines therefore agree with TAG_MAX_COUNT = 20 (file_matching.py:27) and the core's caps. The wording is terse but not wrong.

specification_compliance: I10 is not fully met: the addon and core tag validators can disagree on inputs whose lower() fold changes the string's length (R2-1).
The spec's caps reference at :172 points to section 10, which states 20/200/8 and matches both validators.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Neither validator, nor the spec, says whether the 200-character tag cap applies before or after case-insensitive deduplication.
regression_risks: If the core's fold drifts (for example lower() to casefold()), no core test fails; only the addon-side parity row would notice, and it does not run against the core.
test_coverage: Core TestRequestCaps covers only ASCII deduplication and length caps.
The addon parity table has a casefold row; the core has no counterpart.
not_verified: I did not run any test; the U+0130 divergence was derived by reading the code and from Python's str.lower semantics, not executed.
I did not check whether a FileKindParam enum mismatch exists between the addon and core kind validators beyond the markdown alias.
I did not review the frontend or the search channel changes.
